He was considered one of the top [[National Junior College Athletic Association]] players in the United States while at [[Westchester Community College]] in [[Valhalla, New York]]. ==Early life and career== A native of [[Santo Domingo]], Dominican Republic, Montero played high school basketball at [[Wilbraham & Monson Academy]] in Massachusetts. He then played college basketball for [[Westchester Community College]] in 2013–14 and averaged 15.6 points, 5.9 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game. He returned to Westchester for the 2014–15 season but their season was cancelled due to transcript issues. In January 2015, he enrolled at [[South Plains College]] with the goal of playing for them in 2015–16.{{cite web|first=Brad|last=Winton|title=Luis Montero taking classes at South Plains, will become 2016 JC prospect|url=http://www.jucorecruiting.com/news_article/show/484653-luis-montero-taking-classes-at-south-plains-will-become-2016-jc-prospect|work=JUCORecruiting.com|date=February 27, 2015|accessdate=May 10, 2015}} However, in April 2015, he declared for the [[2015 NBA draft]].{{cite web|last1=Encarnacion|first1=Jose|title=Luis David Montero Se Declara NBA Draft 2015, La Mejor Opcion.!!!|url=http://dominicanosaroybalon.com/luis-david-montero-se-declara-nba-draft-2015-la-mejor-opcion/|work=DominicanosAroYBalon.com|date=April 21, 2015|accessdate=May 10, 2015|language=Spanish}} Montero won a gold medal with his national team at the [[Basketball at the 2023 Central American and Caribbean Games|2023 Central American and Caribbean Games]] held in San Salvador, El Salvador.{{cite news |url=https://www.diariolibre.com/deportes/baloncesto/2023/07/06/dominicana-vence-a-mexico-y-gana-oro-en-san-salvador-2023/2395847 |title=Dominicana vence a México y gana medalla de oro en San Salvador |trans-title=Dominican Republic defeats Mexico and wins gold medal in San Salvador |location=Santo Domingo |publisher=Diario Libre |language=Spanish |date=6 July 2023 |accessdate=26 May 2026}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2015–2016)=== After going undrafted in the [[2015 NBA draft]], Montero joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]]. On July 11, 2015, he signed with the Trail Blazers.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Guard Luis Montero|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-guard-luis-montero|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2015|accessdate=July 11, 2015}} He made his NBA debut on October 30 in a loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]], recording one rebound in two minutes of action.{{cite web|title=Bledsoe, Knight lead Suns to 110-92 win over Portland|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151030/PORPHX/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2015|accessdate=October 30, 2015}} On March 10, 2016, using the flexible assignment rule, he was assigned to the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]], the [[NBA G League|D-League]] affiliate of the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Assign Cliff Alexander and Luis Montero to Santa Cruz Warriors|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/trail-blazers-assign-cliff-alexander-and-luis-montero-to-santa-cruz-warriors/n-5109694|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 10, 2016|accessdate=March 10, 2016}} On March 20, he was recalled by Portland.{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Richman|title=Trail Blazers recall Luis Montero, Cliff Alexander from NBA Development League|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2016/03/trail_blazers_recall_luis_montero_cliff_alexander.html|work=OregonLive.com|date=March 20, 2016|accessdate=March 24, 2016}} On October 15, 2016, he was waived by the Trail Blazers.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Waive Luis Montero|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-waive-luis-montero|work=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2016|accessdate=October 15, 2016}} ===NBA D League (2016–17)=== On October 18, 2016, Montero signed with the [[Miami Heat]],{{cite web|title=Heat Signs Luis Montero|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/heat-signs-luis-montero|work=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2016|accessdate=October 18, 2016}} but was waived on October 22 after appearing in two preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waives-five-players|title=Heat Waives Five Players|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2016|accessdate=October 22, 2016}} On November 1, 2016, he was acquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Heat.{{cite web|url=http://siouxfalls.dleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announce-2016-training-camp-roster/|title=Skyforce Announce 2016 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 1, 2016|accessdate=November 3, 2016|archive-date=November 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104075937/http://siouxfalls.dleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announce-2016-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} On March 2, 2017, Montero was traded to the [[Stockton Kings|Reno Bighorns]].{{cite web|url=http://reno.dleague.nba.com/news/bighorns-acquire-montero-2017-draft-selection/|title=Bighorns Acquire Montero and 2017 Draft Selection|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive|date=March 2, 2017|accessdate=March 3, 2017}} ===NBA D League and return to South America (2017–18)=== Montero was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the NBA. Under the terms of the deal, he split time between the Pistons and their G-League affiliate, the [[Grand Rapids Drive]]. On January 13, 2018, Montero was waived by the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=http://gleague.nba.com/news/detroit-pistons-sign-guards-kay-felder-reggie-hearn-two-way-contracts/|title=Detroit Pistons Sign Guards Kay Felder And Reggie Hearn To Two-Way Contracts|work=NBA.com|date=January 15, 2018|accessdate=January 15, 2018}} On January 27, 2018, Montero was reacquired by the [[Stockton Kings|Reno Bighorns]],{{cite web|url=http://reno.gleague.nba.com/news/reno-bighorns-reacquire-luis-montero/|title=Reno Bighorns Reacquire Luis Montero|work=NBA.com|date=January 27, 2018|accessdate=January 27, 2018}} but was waived in March. In March 2018, Montero signed with ''El Millõn Yireh'', a basketball team in the second tier of the Dominican Basketball League ''Torebonde Baloncesto Superior'' (TBS). He made his debut on March 27, in a 87–74 loss to ''Huellas del Siglo'', and left the club at the end of the year. ===Poland and Mexico (2018–19)=== On August 9, 2018, Montero signed with [[KK Włocławek|Anwil Włocławek]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]].{{cite web |title=Luis Montero signs with Anwil Wloclawek |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/europe/poland/285192/luis-montero-signs-with-anwil-wloclawek.html |publisher=Sportando |accessdate=August 9, 2018 |date=August 9, 2018}} After a few days Montero was fired by Anwil due to his failure to undergo medical tests. On January 11, 2019, Montero was reported to have signed with [[Mexico City Capitanes|Capitanes de Ciudad de México]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]] (LNBP) for one month.{{cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/luis-montero-signs-a-one-month-deal-with-capitanes-de-ciudad-de-mexico/|title=Luis Montero signs a one-month deal with Capitanes de Ciudad de Mexico|date=January 11, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|accessdate=January 11, 2019}} ===Argentina (2019–present)=== In October 2019, Montero signed with [[Argentina|Argentinian]] team [[Club Atlético Platense]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.webasketball.com.ar/platense-incorporo-a-luis-montero/|title=Platense incorporó a Luis Montero – Web Basketball}} In October 2020, he signed with [[San Lorenzo (basketball)|San Lorenzo]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Básquet]], Argentina.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basquetplus.com/san-lorenzo-bcla-lnb|title = San Lorenzo, completo: Llegó Luis Montero y ya tiene a
